Krasnik Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kraśnik, Poland

Demolished. Kraśnik's first Jewish cemetery, established around the turn of the 17th century and first documented in 1612, was closed in the 1640s or 1650s — reportedly because townspeople complained about funeral processions passing noisily through the market square, prompting communal buildings to relocate elsewhere in town. During WWII its tombstones were pulled up and used to pave streets, and today no trace of the cemetery survives beyond a single tombstone, dated 1634, that was preserved outside the original grounds. It served one of Poland's older Jewish communities, present here from the late 16th century and numbering nearly two-thirds of the town's population by 1787.
